US-01
As a restaurant owner, I want to register my restaurant with its name, logo, address and business hours, so that I can start setting up on Sufria without engineering support.

Required fields validated before submission.
An incomplete profile can be saved as a draft and resumed.
On success the restaurant is created with status "trial".
FR-01
US-02
As a restaurant owner or staff member, I want to create, edit and delete menu categories and items myself, so that the menu stays accurate without contacting the Sufria team.

Adding or editing an item requires at minimum a name, price and availability flag.
Marking an item unavailable hides it from the bot without deleting its order history.
An invalid price or missing field is rejected with a clear message.
FR-02
US-03
As a platform, I want to provision a dedicated WhatsApp Business number for each restaurant, so that every restaurant has its own independent verified ordering channel.

Provisioning starts once verification documents are submitted.
whatsapp_verification_status accurately reflects verified / pending / rejected.
A delay beyond the 2-5 business day window (up to 30) notifies the restaurant with guidance.
FR-03
US-04
As a restaurant owner, I want to customise my welcome and notification templates, so that customers get a branded experience within WhatsApp's rules.

A default platform template is used if the owner does not customise.
Custom templates are submitted to Meta for approval before going live.
A rejected template notifies the owner so the wording can be revised.
FR-04
US-05
As a customer, I want to be greeted with the current menu the moment I message the restaurant, so that I can start ordering immediately.

A first message with no active session creates one.
A redelivered webhook does not create a second session or resend the menu.
Messaging during an active session resumes at the current step instead of restarting.
FR-05
US-06
As a customer, I want to browse categories and add items using buttons or lists, so that ordering feels like a normal WhatsApp chat.

Selection uses interactive buttons and lists wherever possible, not free text.
The cart persists in the session context as items are added.
Off-script free text gets a brief clarification without losing the cart.
FR-06
US-07
As a customer, I want to review my full cart and total before paying, so that I can catch mistakes before committing.

The summary shows every item, quantity and the order total.
Prices and availability are re-validated at this step; any change is shown for re-confirmation.
An emptied cart returns me to browsing rather than an empty summary.
FR-07
US-08
As a returning customer, I want the bot to proactively suggest my usual order the moment I message, so that getting my usual is effortless rather than merely fast.

A customer with a prior completed order sees the suggestion inside the welcome message itself.
Every suggested item's price and availability is re-validated before the suggestion is shown.
Confirming jumps straight to cart review; dismissing proceeds through normal browsing.
FR-08 (highest business priority)
US-09
As a customer, I want to choose pickup or delivery, so that I get my food the way that works for me.

Only the fulfilment options the restaurant supports are shown.
The selection is recorded on the order as fulfillment_type.
FR-09
US-10
As a customer, I want to pay online or choose cash on delivery, so that I can use whichever method I trust.

The order is created the moment I choose a method — online or cash — not once payment confirms.
Online payment sends a provider-hosted instrument; the order shows pending until confirmed.
If payment fails or expires I can retry or switch to cash on the same order.
If I never complete payment within 2 hours the order is cancelled and I am told payment was not completed in time — not that I was late.
No cardholder data is ever stored on Sufria's infrastructure.
US-11
As a customer, I want automatic WhatsApp updates as my order progresses, so that I know what is happening without asking.

A status change (accepted, preparing, ready, cancelled, expired, completed) triggers a matching template.
A failed delivery is retried with backoff; persistent failure raises a monitoring alert.
FR-11
US-12
As a restaurant staff member, I want incoming and in-progress orders to update automatically, so that I do not refresh the page during a rush.

The live-orders view polls every 3-5 seconds while visible.
A connectivity issue shows a clear warning rather than failing silently.
FR-12
US-13

As a restaurant staff member, I want to accept, cancel or progress an order in one click with every change recorded, so that I can run the kitchen without friction and have an audit trail if anything is disputed.

Only valid transitions are allowed for the current state.
For an online order, Accept is unavailable until payment_status = paid; Cancel is the only action before that.
Every change is written to an append-only history: who or what, from which status to which, when, and why for a cancellation.
Cancelling a paid order — or a pickup expiring, or a 2-hour payment timeout — triggers exactly one refund even if a payment confirmation arrives at nearly the same moment.
Marking a cash order completed moves payment_status from pending_cash to collected.
A pickup left in ready for 24 hours moves to expired, separately from a completed handover.
FR-13
US-14
As a platform, I want each customer's order count, spend and VIP status kept current automatically, so that restaurants can recognise their best customers without bookkeeping.

Completing an order updates total_orders, total_spend and last_order_at.
is_vip is recalculated against the threshold on every completion.
An expired order never updates these statistics, regardless of payment status.
FR-14
US-15
As a restaurant owner, I want a flat monthly fee instead of a per-order commission, so that my costs stay predictable as volume grows.

Billing runs automatically at the start of each cycle.
A failed charge moves the subscription to past_due and notifies the owner.
FR-16
US-16
As a restaurant owner, I want my order count, revenue and repeat-customer percentage at a glance, so that I can judge how the platform performs for my business.

Analytics load within 3 seconds for the selected range.
A period with no orders shows a clear empty state rather than an error.
FR-17
US-17

As a restaurant owner, I want one combined score showing how much revenue comes from direct repeat customers and roughly how much commission I am saving, so that I see the return without doing the maths myself.

The score combines percentage of revenue from direct repeat customers with estimated commission saved, based on a configurable assumed_commission_rate.
With too few orders the figure is shown next to its sample size rather than hidden, so it never implies false precision.
FR-18
US-18
As a restaurant owner, I want a funnel of how many customers started, browsed and paid, so that I can find where I am losing orders.

Session counts are shown per stage with drop-off between consecutive stages.
A period with no sessions shows a clear empty state.
FR-19
US-19
As a restaurant owner, I want one customer's order history and VIP changes on a single timeline, so that I understand that relationship at a glance.

The timeline merges order history and VIP-tier changes chronologically for one customer.
Cancelled and expired orders appear in the timeline even though they are excluded from the summary statistics.
FR-20
US-20
As a restaurant owner, I want customers who have gone quiet flagged against their usual pattern, so that I can decide myself whether to win them back.

A customer is flagged only once they have enough history for a reliable baseline.
The system never sends any message automatically — flagging is for awareness only.
FR-21
US-21
As a restaurant staff member, I want to log in securely to the dashboard, so that only authorised people can see my restaurant's orders and customer data.

Login requires a valid identifier and password; the session is maintained with JWT and refresh tokens.
Access is checked per restaurant membership on every request, not merely per user.
An expired or invalid session redirects to login rather than exposing stale data.
NFR-02 — no FR exists. Proposed FR-23
US-22
As a restaurant owner, I want to search and view my full customer list with order count, spend and VIP status, so that I can act on this data instead of leaving it in the database.

The list is searchable and filterable by name or phone number.
VIP customers are visibly flagged.
Distinct from FR-20: this is the list view a staff member lands on first.
Scope §1.5.1 and FR-14 data — no FR exists. Proposed FR-24
US-23
As a restaurant owner, I want the bot to reflect whether my restaurant is currently open, so that customers cannot place orders the kitchen cannot fulfil.

Outside the configured business_hours the bot shows a clearly worded closed message instead of starting the ordering flow.
The check runs before the menu is sent, not after a cart is built.
An empty business_hours configuration is treated as always open.
FR-01 (business_hours) and FR-05 — no rule exists. Proposed FR-22
